title: Race Bib Exchange
tagline: Organiser-approved transfers of sold-out Thai race entries, with escrow and a face-value price cap
problem: Popular Thai road races and trail events now sell out within hours: the 2026 Pattaya Marathon filled 21,727 places from 58 countries in about two hours. Runners who get injured, change jobs or cannot travel are left holding a ฿1,000-3,000 (est.) entry, while thousands of others who missed the window hunt for bibs in Facebook groups and LINE chats. Those informal swaps invite scams (paying by transfer for a bib that never arrives), unofficial bib-swaps that break organiser rules and void insurance, and scalping. Organisers that do allow transfers handle them by email or one-off forms with fees and deadlines, such as the ฿500 fee UTMB Chiang Mai has charged, so most entries are simply wasted.
solution: A transfer marketplace that organisers plug into: a seller lists an entry, a buyer on the waitlist claims it, and the platform performs the official name change through the organiser's registration system (ThaiRun-style platforms or a CSV/API handshake) so the new runner is properly insured and timed. Payment is held in escrow via PromptPay and only released once the organiser confirms the name change, which ends Facebook-transfer scams. Prices are capped at face value plus a small fee, and organisers set their own transfer windows and take a revenue share instead of handling emails. An LLM assistant handles bilingual eligibility checks (age, qualifying times for trail races, shirt-size swaps) and answers runner questions on LINE. For runners, one waitlist across every race replaces refreshing dozens of groups; for organisers, it means fuller start lines, less admin and real no-show data.
target_audience: Thai recreational runners aged 25-45; expat and foreign destination runners; road and trail race organisers; corporate running clubs
business_model: Transaction fee per transfer (buyer) + organiser revenue share + optional organiser SaaS for waitlists
pricing: Buyer fee ฿99-199 per transfer; seller lists free; organiser waitlist module ฿4,900 per event (or free with 30% share of transfer fees)
score_justification: L3 AI does bilingual eligibility/support, core is marketplace plumbing; E4 escrow + listings + organiser CSV in ~4 wks; A4 races selling out in hours; P4 running Facebook groups, LINE OA, Strava clubs; M4 transfer, no-show and demand data per race; W3 runners pay small fees, organisers pay only if it saves admin
platform_distribution: Thai running Facebook groups and pages; LINE OA; Strava clubs; organiser partnerships; TikTok running creators
tam_source: bottom-up: est. 400 sizeable Thai races/yr × est. 3% of entries transferable × avg 5,000 entries = 60,000 transfers × ฿150 ≈ ฿9M fees + organiser modules 400 × ฿4,900 ≈ ฿2M + foreign-runner premium transfers est. ฿4M ≈ ฿15M (est.)
competitors: ThaiRun (race registration); organiser email/form transfers (e.g. UTMB Chiang Mai); Facebook bib-swap groups; Running Connect-style registration platforms
competitor_gap: Registration platforms sell first entries but do not run cross-race waitlists or escrowed name changes; Facebook swaps have no escrow or organiser approval
demand_evidence: Pattaya Mail reports the 2026 Pattaya Marathon sold out in about two hours with 21,727 runners from 58 countries, and Running Magazine describes a Thai running boom where races sell out well in advance. UTMB Chiang Mai publishes a paid transfer process, showing organisers accept transfers when they are controlled.
unique_data_capture: Per-race transfer volumes, waitlist depth, no-show rates and resale demand by distance and date; lets organisers price and size future editions and compounds with every race season
commoditization_risk: Medium: a registration platform such as ThaiRun could add transfers, but cross-platform waitlists and escrow need neutral organiser buy-in
regulatory_notes: Escrow-style holding of funds may touch Bank of Thailand e-payment rules; use a licensed payment provider's split/escrow features. PDPA consent for sharing runner ID data with organisers. Respect organiser terms; never facilitate transfers on races that ban them.
founder_feasibility: Foreign Business Act: operating a marketplace or booking platform inside Thailand is an 'other service' under List 3, so a foreign founder needs a Thai company with >=51% Thai shareholding, a Foreign Business Licence, or BOI promotion (digital platform/software activities are promotable); an offshore entity can run the platform cross-border at first, but local PromptPay escrow and organiser contracts are easier through a Thai company. A Work Permit is still needed to work on it physically in Thailand. Solo-feasible: one founder plus organiser partnerships; customer support via LINE OA.
payment_rails: PromptPay QR + cards (Omise/2C2P) with delayed payout; Stripe for foreign buyers
mvp_features: Entry listing with organiser verification; cross-race waitlist and alerts; PromptPay escrow released on name-change confirmation; face-value price cap; organiser dashboard with CSV export; LINE OA bot for status
tech_stack: Next.js + Supabase + LINE Messaging API + payment provider API (Omise/2C2P) + LLM API (Claude/GPT)
review_notes: Biggest risk is organiser adoption: without official name-change support it becomes another unofficial swap board.

title: Driving School Compare
tagline: Compare DLT-certified driving schools by all-in price, pass rate and next start date, in Thai and English
problem: Getting a first Thai driving licence means either queuing for DLT training and tests or paying a DLT-certified private school, where a 15-hour car course costs roughly ฿3,500-6,500 and a motorcycle course ฿1,000-2,000. Each school bundles different things (exam fees, retests, certificate fees, manual vs automatic cars, weekend slots), so the headline price rarely matches the final bill. Learners, parents of 18-year-olds and foreigners who cannot convert a home licence compare schools through scattered Facebook pages, Google Maps reviews and listicles that recommend a handful of chains. Nobody publishes which schools actually have certification, open slots next week, an English-speaking instructor, or a good first-time pass rate.
solution: A bilingual directory and booking marketplace for DLT-certified driving schools, starting with Bangkok, Nonthaburi, Pathum Thani, Chiang Mai and Phuket. Each listing shows the verified certification status, an itemised all-in price per course (car auto/manual, motorcycle, refresher), what is included (written and practical tests, free retest, certificate), next start dates and language of instruction. Learners book and pay a deposit through the platform, and after the course they report pass or fail on each test, building first-time pass rates per school. An LLM assistant answers questions in Thai and English (documents a foreigner needs, medical certificate, which route is cheaper for an experienced driver) and pre-fills applications. Schools pay a commission only on confirmed bookings, which beats paying for Facebook ads.
target_audience: Thai 18-22 year-olds and their parents; adults learning to drive later; foreigners needing a first Thai licence; companies training motorbike delivery riders
business_model: Marketplace commission on bookings + featured listings for schools
pricing: Free for learners; school commission 8% of course fee (about ฿300-500 per car booking); featured listing ฿1,990/month
score_justification: L2 AI only for Q&A and price normalisation; E4 directory + booking ~3 wks; A4 every new driver needs a licence and searches 'โรงเรียนสอนขับรถ'; P4 Google Maps/SEO, TikTok, Pantip; M3 verified pass-rate and price history per school; W3 schools pay commission but are fragmented
platform_distribution: Google SEO for 'โรงเรียนสอนขับรถ + district'; Google Maps; TikTok learner-driver content; Pantip; expat Facebook groups
tam_source: bottom-up: est. 400,000 learners/yr using private schools × avg ฿4,500 course = ฿1.8B course spend × 8% commission ≈ ฿144M (est.)
competitors: KTC and other listicle guides; Google Maps; school Facebook pages; chains such as Advance Bangkok; self-study DLT route
competitor_gap: No source verifies certification, itemises all-in prices, shows live start dates or publishes pass rates; listicles cover a handful of chains
demand_evidence: Sanook reported that new licence rules moved 15 hours of training to about 90 DLT-supervised private schools at up to ฿6,000, and PPTV reported complaints about the extra ฿5,000-6,000 cost. KTC's guide lists price ranges of ฿3,500-6,500 and tells readers to ask schools directly about certification, showing the information gap.
unique_data_capture: Learner-reported first-time pass rates per school and test type, itemised price history and slot availability; improves with every booking and is hard for listicles to copy
commoditization_risk: Medium: Google Maps covers discovery and DLT could publish a school list, but neither shows pass rates, prices or bookings
regulatory_notes: Must not claim DLT endorsement; verify certification against DLT lists. PDPA consent for learner ID documents. Pass-rate data must be clearly labelled as self-reported.
founder_feasibility: Foreign Business Act: operating a directory and booking marketplace inside Thailand is an 'other service' under List 3, so a foreign founder needs a Thai company with >=51% Thai shareholding, a Foreign Business Licence, or BOI promotion (digital platform/software activities are promotable); an offshore entity can sell featured listings cross-border, but collecting learner deposits in THB is simpler through a Thai company. A Work Permit is still needed to work on it physically in Thailand. Solo-feasible, but onboarding schools needs a Thai-speaking partner or sales hire.
payment_rails: PromptPay QR + cards (Omise/2C2P); bank transfer for school payouts
mvp_features: Certified-school directory with itemised prices; next start dates and booking deposit; learner pass/fail reporting; bilingual Q&A on documents and routes; school dashboard for slots and prices
tech_stack: Next.js + Supabase + LLM API (Claude/GPT) + Google Maps API + LINE Login
review_notes: Distinct from TH-008 (foreign licence conversion slots); the main risk is schools refusing commission and listing only on Facebook.

title: Durian Export Lot Ledger
tagline: Links every durian container to its GAP orchard and BY2/cadmium lab report before it ships to China
problem: Thailand shipped 982,016 tonnes of durian worth about ฿125.9B in 2025, almost all to China, and every container now needs a registered GAP orchard, a registered GMP packing house and a lab report clearing BY2 dye and cadmium. In January 2025 around 100 containers were reportedly sent back for missing BY2 results, and the Department of Agriculture suspended certificates for several packing houses after detections. Packing houses still match orchard codes, harvest lots, lab PDFs and phytosanitary paperwork in LINE chats and Excel, so one mislabelled lot can suspend an entire orchard code or exporter. Small and mid-size packing houses cannot afford the bespoke systems that large exporters build.
solution: A lot ledger for packing houses and exporters that records, per pallet and container, which registered orchard code each lot came from, the harvest date and maturity check, and the matching lab report. Orchard suppliers send harvest photos and delivery notes through a LINE OA; the system reads orchard GAP certificates and lab-report PDFs, checks registration numbers and expiry dates, and blocks a container from being marked ready until every lot has a valid BY2 and cadmium result. It produces the document pack and QR trace page that buyers and Chinese importers ask for, and flags suppliers whose lots repeatedly fail or arrive without paperwork. Unlike research prototypes or GS1 pilots, it is built for a 20-person packing house in Chanthaburi or Chumphon, works on phones in Thai, and costs less than one rejected container.
target_audience: Durian packing houses (lhong) in Chanthaburi, Rayong, Trat, Chumphon and Surat Thani; small and mid-size fruit exporters; durian cooperatives; Chinese importers auditing Thai suppliers
business_model: Subscription per packing house + per-container document fee in peak season
pricing: Starter ฿2,990/month (1 packing house, 50 containers/season); Pro ฿7,900/month (multi-site, importer portal); ฿150 per extra container; cooperative plan ฿19,900/season
score_justification: L4 AI reads lab PDFs, GAP certs and delivery notes; E3 LINE OA + document parsing + lot model ~6 wks with field testing; A4 rejected containers and lab rules widely reported; P3 LINE OA, exporter associations, packing-house networks, no app-store pull; M5 orchard-level lot and lab-result history across seasons; W4 one rejected container costs far more than a year's fee
platform_distribution: LINE OA; durian exporter and packing-house associations in Chanthaburi and Chumphon; provincial agriculture offices; Facebook durian trade groups
tam_source: bottom-up: est. 1,500 registered durian packing houses × ฿60,000/yr ≈ ฿90M + per-container fees on est. 60,000 containers × ฿150 ≈ ฿9M; ≈ ฿100M (est.) before longan/mangosteen expansion
competitors: Digital Durian initiative (depa) tools; BIOTEC-NECTEC GAP durian traceability project; Thai-Chinese Chamber of Commerce/CCIC QR traceability service; GS1 Thailand pilots; Excel + LINE
competitor_gap: Government and research systems focus on orchard records or consumer QR codes; none blocks a container until every lot has a matching valid lab report and certificate, priced for small packing houses
demand_evidence: The Star (Jan 2026) reports orchards and packing houses must register with the Department of Agriculture for China exports, and 2025 export value fell to ฿125.868B despite higher volume. Reporting in January 2025 described about 100 containers returned for missing BY2 results, and Pattaya Mail reported GACC cadmium alerts that suspended packing houses and GAP orchards.
unique_data_capture: Season-by-season lot records linking orchard codes to lab results, rejection events and supplier reliability; becomes a risk score for orchards that importers and lenders would pay for
commoditization_risk: Medium: depa, the Department of Agriculture or CCIC could expand free tools, but they serve regulators and consumers rather than packing-house workflow
regulatory_notes: Tool records compliance; it does not issue phytosanitary certificates or replace DOA/GACC registration. PDPA for farmer ID data. Lab results must be shown as issued, never edited.
founder_feasibility: Foreign Business Act: operating a software service for Thai businesses inside Thailand is an 'other service' under List 3, so a foreign founder needs a Thai company with >=51% Thai shareholding, a Foreign Business Licence, or BOI promotion (digital platform/software activities are promotable); selling SaaS cross-border from an offshore entity is the simplest legal start, with a Thai reseller for invoicing in THB. A Work Permit is still needed to work on it physically in Thailand. A solo technical founder needs a Thai-speaking field partner in Chanthaburi for the durian season (roughly April-August) to onboard packing houses.
payment_rails: Bank transfer with e-Tax Invoice; PromptPay QR; cards (Omise/2C2P)
mvp_features: LINE OA intake of orchard deliveries with photos; GAP/GMP certificate and lab-report PDF parsing with expiry checks; lot-to-container mapping with a ready/blocked gate; export document pack and QR trace page; supplier failure dashboard
tech_stack: Next.js + Supabase + LINE Messaging API + OCR + LLM API (Claude/GPT)
review_notes: Must confirm with packing houses which documents GACC and DOA actually check today, as rules have changed repeatedly since 2024.

title: Solo 401k Limit Planner
tagline: Tracks day-job and side-business 401(k) contributions together so you max out without an excess deferral
problem: Many Americans (est. millions) pair a W-2 job with consulting, creator or 1099 income, and a Solo 401(k) lets them shelter far more than an IRA: in 2026 the employee deferral limit is $24,500 shared across every 401(k) they hold, plus an employer contribution of up to 25% of compensation. The IRS says the deferral limit is per person, not per plan, and no plan administrator can see contributions made elsewhere, so the owner must track it alone. Mistakes are common: excess deferrals can be taxed twice, the employer contribution for sole proprietors depends on net earnings after half of self-employment tax, and once plan assets pass $250,000 a missed Form 5500-EZ costs $250 a day. Spreadsheet calculators give a one-off number but do not follow pay stubs and income during the year.
solution: A planner that links (or reads uploaded) pay stubs and the side business's books, and keeps a running year-to-date view of deferrals across every plan. It calculates the remaining employee deferral room, the maximum employer contribution for a sole proprietor or S-corp from actual net earnings and age-based catch-up limits. Before each deposit it shows a safe amount and generates the contribution memo for the plan provider. At year end it tracks the $250,000 Form 5500-EZ threshold, reminds the owner of the July 31 deadline and pre-fills the form data. It also produces a one-page summary for the owner's CPA. Unlike plan providers' calculators, it updates with every pay stub and works with any custodian (Fidelity, Schwab, E*TRADE, Carry, Ubiquity).
target_audience: W-2 employees with side consulting or creator income; self-employed professionals with a Solo 401(k); S-corp owner-operators; physicians and engineers with 1099 moonlighting
pricing: Free calculator; Pro $79/year (tracking, alerts, 5500-EZ prep); CPA plan $29/client/year
score_justification: L4 AI reads pay stubs and P&L, does the limit math; E4 parsing + rules engine ~3 wks; A3 recurring forum questions but niche; P3 SEO, FIRE/physician communities, CPA referrals; M2 limited proprietary data; W3 prosumers pay for tax tools but free calculators exist
platform_distribution: Google SEO ('solo 401k contribution with W-2 401k'); Reddit/Bogleheads/FIRE communities; White Coat Investor-style physician audiences; CPA referrals
tam_source: bottom-up: est. 750,000 Solo 401(k) owners with another income source × $79/yr ≈ $59M (est.)
competitors: Carry (Solo 401k with tracking guidance); Best Solo 401k multi-401k calculator; Fidelity/Schwab Solo 401k calculators; TurboTax/H&R Block; CPA spreadsheets
competitor_gap: Calculators give a static one-off answer; providers only see their own plan; none tracks deferrals across employers through the year and handles the 5500-EZ threshold
demand_evidence: TurboTax community threads ask whether TurboTax correctly calculates the maximum Solo 401k contribution when the user also has a W-2 employer plan. Carry's guide says owners, not employers, must track combined deferrals, and calculator sites dedicated to multi-401k limits exist.
unique_data_capture: Anonymised patterns of mixed W-2 and self-employment income and contribution timing; modest value, mainly for product tuning
commoditization_risk: Medium: custodians like Carry could add cross-plan tracking and general AI assistants can do the math once, but continuous pay-stub tracking is not offered
regulatory_notes: Must be framed as tax calculation software, not personalised investment advice (avoid recommending securities to stay outside investment-adviser registration). Store pay-stub data under GLBA-style safeguards.
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible as a US LLC or offshore SaaS selling via Stripe; rules engine needs annual updates when IRS limits change and a CPA reviewer on contract.
mvp_features: Pay stub and P&L upload with extraction; cross-plan YTD deferral tracker; employer contribution calculator (sole prop and S-corp); safe-deposit alerts; Form 5500-EZ threshold and deadline tracker; CPA summary export
tech_stack: Next.js + Supabase + OCR + LLM API (Claude/GPT) + Plaid (optional)
review_notes: Thin moat and free calculators make this a CAUTION; best as a feature sold through CPAs or a custodian partnership.

title: Write Off Valuation Challenger
tagline: Car written off? Get its fair market value with evidence and a ready-to-send challenge to your insurer
problem: When a car is written off, UK insurers pay the market value just before the loss, usually set from trade guides, and many owners receive offers that will not buy a comparable car. Disputed car values are a major source of motor insurance complaints: the Financial Ombudsman has published hundreds of decisions where offers rose after challenge, sometimes with 8% interest added. Owners rarely know that the Ombudsman checks the insurer's method against several valuation guides and comparable adverts, that deductions for prior write-off categories can be challenged, or what evidence wins. MoneySavingExpert threads show the same pattern repeatedly: owners who push back with proof get more, while most accept the first offer within days.
solution: The owner enters the registration, mileage, condition and options, and uploads the insurer's offer letter. The tool pulls comparable adverts for the same model, year, mileage and spec, adjusts for differences, and shows where the offer sits against the range the Ombudsman typically uses. It drafts a formal challenge letter citing the policy's market-value wording and FOS approach, flags deductions that need justification (salvage retained, prior Category N/S write-off cuts, recovery and storage charges) and sets reminders for the insurer's 8-week final-response deadline. If the insurer will not move, it assembles an Ombudsman complaint pack with the evidence. Outcome data from users shows which insurers raise offers and by how much, which no guide or forum offers.
target_audience: UK drivers with a total-loss claim; owners of modified, rare or high-spec cars; motorcyclists; families relying on one car
business_model: Pay per case with optional success fee
pricing: Free valuation check; Challenge pack £29; Ombudsman pack £49; optional 10% of any uplift above the first offer, capped at £250
score_justification: L4 AI finds and adjusts comparables and drafts letters; E4 adverts + letter templates ~3 wks; A4 large volume of FOS decisions and MSE threads; P3 SEO and MSE-style forums, no built-in channel; M4 offer vs settled value data by insurer and model; W3 one-off payers with uplift at stake
platform_distribution: Google SEO ('car written off valuation too low'); MoneySavingExpert and Mumsnet threads; car owner clubs and forums; partnerships with independent engineers
tam_source: bottom-up: est. 500,000 UK total-loss claims/yr × est. 15% disputing × £60 avg revenue (pack + capped success fee) ≈ £4.5M (est.)
competitors: Free FOS complaint route; Parkers/Glass's/CAP HPI valuation tools; MoneySavingExpert guides and forums; independent engineers' valuation reports; claims management companies
competitor_gap: Valuation tools give a guide price but not evidence formatted for an insurer or FOS; engineers are costly; forums give anecdotes, not outcomes by insurer
demand_evidence: Insurance Edge reported, citing FOS data, that car and motorcycle insurance complaints rose 27% in 2022-23 with disputed values a key driver. FOS decision DRN-3704117 (U K Insurance, claim value) records a change in outcome, and MSE threads such as 'Low insurance valuation offered on car to be written off' recur.
unique_data_capture: First offer, challenge evidence and final settlement by insurer, model, age and mileage; reveals systematic under-valuation and compounds with every case
commoditization_risk: Medium: a general AI assistant can draft a letter, but comparable-advert matching and insurer outcome data are not built in
regulatory_notes: Helping consumers pursue insurance claims for a fee may be a regulated claims management activity in Great Britain (FCA authorisation); a self-serve document tool without representation reduces but may not remove this, so take legal advice. Success fees would very likely require CMC authorisation. GDPR for claim documents.
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible as a UK Ltd; start with flat-fee self-serve packs while the FCA claims-management question is checked; advert data needs a licensed feed or partnership.
mvp_features: Offer letter upload and parsing; comparable-advert finder with adjustments; valuation range vs offer chart; challenge letter generator; 8-week deadline tracker; Ombudsman complaint pack
tech_stack: Next.js + Supabase + vehicle data API (DVLA/MOT) + advert data feed + LLM API (Claude/GPT)
review_notes: Biggest open question is whether FCA claims-management rules force authorisation before any success fee can be charged.

title: PPDS Label Change Guard
tagline: Keeps Natasha's Law labels correct when wholesalers change an ingredient, for cafes, bakeries and delis
problem: Since October 2021 any UK business that makes food and packs it before sale on the same premises (sandwiches, salads, cakes, deli pots) must label it with a full ingredients list and the 14 allergens emphasised. The labels are only as good as the recipe data behind them: when a wholesaler swaps a bread, sauce or spice blend, the sub-ingredients change and the printed label becomes wrong, which is how allergic customers get hurt. An FSA-commissioned evaluation found nearly a quarter of businesses surveyed admitted non-compliance, and most local authorities said more action was needed. Label printers and apps cost £13-34 a month, but they print what staff type in; none watches the supplier side.
solution: Staff photograph or forward supplier product specs and delivery notes, and the system extracts each product's ingredients and allergens into a recipe library. Recipes are built from those products, and the tool generates compliant PPDS labels in the FSA format, which print on the label printer the business already owns. The key feature is change detection: every new delivery note, invoice line or supplier spec is compared with the stored version, and if a product code, brand or ingredient list changes, the affected recipes and labels are flagged before the next print run. An audit log shows the EHO when each label was last checked and against which spec. It is sold as an add-on for small food businesses that already have a printer, not another printer contract.
target_audience: Independent cafes and coffee shops; bakeries; delis and farm shops; school and workplace caterers; market traders selling prepacked food
pricing: Starter £19/month (1 site, 50 recipes); Pro £39/month (unlimited recipes, multi-site, audit log); £149 one-off recipe import service
score_justification: L4 AI extracts supplier specs and compares versions; E3 spec parsing + label templates + printer support ~6 wks; A3 legal duty but low search for change monitoring; P3 trade bodies (NCASS), wholesalers, EHO advice; M4 supplier product-spec change database across thousands of SKUs; W4 businesses already pay £13-34/month for label tools
platform_distribution: Trade bodies (NCASS, Craft Bakers Association); wholesaler partnerships; Google SEO ('Natasha's Law labels'); local authority food safety newsletters
tam_source: bottom-up: est. 80,000 UK sites selling PPDS food × est. 30% adopting × £29/month × 12 ≈ £8.4M (est.)
competitors: Labl.it; Planglow LabelLogic Live; Food Alert Assure65 PPDS; Brother/Toshiba TEC free label software; Nutritics
competitor_gap: Existing tools print labels from manually entered recipes; none monitors supplier specs and delivery notes for ingredient changes that silently invalidate labels
demand_evidence: The FSA PPDS evaluation, reported by The Grocer, found nearly a quarter of food businesses surveyed admitted non-compliance and 75% of local authorities believed further action was needed. Label tools such as Labl.it already charge about £28-34 a month, showing businesses pay for PPDS compliance.
unique_data_capture: Versioned ingredient and allergen specs for wholesaler products with change dates; each new customer's deliveries extend coverage and it could later be licensed to wholesalers and caterers
commoditization_risk: Medium: label vendors could add spec monitoring and wholesalers could push data feeds, but no one owns the cross-wholesaler change history
regulatory_notes: The food business remains legally responsible for labels; the product must disclaim liability and require human sign-off. Errors could contribute to allergic reactions, so professional indemnity insurance is needed. Applies to England, Wales and NI with Scottish equivalent rules.
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible as a UK Ltd; needs a food-safety consultant to review label templates and early pilots with 10-20 cafes.
mvp_features: Supplier spec and delivery-note photo extraction; recipe builder with allergen roll-up; FSA-format PPDS label generator for common printers; ingredient change detection and alerts; EHO audit log
tech_stack: Next.js + Supabase + OCR + LLM API (Claude/GPT) + label printer SDKs (Brother/Zebra)
review_notes: Distinct from TH-065 (tourist menu translation); liability for a missed allergen is the biggest risk and needs insurance and mandatory human sign-off.

title: Packaging EPR Data Builder
tagline: Turns your SKU list and supplier specs into the packaging data UK small producers must report under EPR
problem: UK packaging EPR now obliges any business with over £1 million turnover that supplies more than 25 tonnes of packaging to register and report its packaging by material, class and weight, with 2026 data due by 1 April 2027. Small producers pay a registration fee of £1,303 direct or £696 through a compliance scheme, and a £386 late fee if they miss registration. The hard part is the data: weights per SKU and per component (box, film, label, tape) sit with suppliers and 3PLs, and founders of D2C brands, food producers and importers rebuild it in spreadsheets each year. Compliance schemes charge for data services and do not publish prices, so small producers either overpay or guess.
solution: A self-serve data builder that imports the product catalogue from Shopify, Amazon or an Excel SKU list and sales volumes from the ecommerce platform. For each SKU it reads supplier spec sheets and invoices, and where no spec exists it guides the user through weighing a sample with a phone photo and kitchen scale, then suggests material and packaging class codes. It rolls weights up by material, activity (brand owner, importer, packer/filler) and nation of sale into the file layout the government reporting service expects, with an evidence log for each figure. It also flags packaging that is likely to face higher fees for large producers in future (mixed materials, dark plastics), so growing brands can redesign before they cross the £2 million or 50-tonne line. Unlike compliance-scheme data services, it is priced for a small producer and the business keeps its own data.
target_audience: UK D2C and Shopify brands over £1m turnover; small food and drink producers; importers of consumer goods; Amazon FBA sellers with UK packaging
pricing: Small producer £390/year (up to 200 SKUs); Growth £890/year (up to 1,000 SKUs, multiple brands); £250 one-off onboarding
score_justification: L4 AI reads specs and suggests material codes; E3 catalogue import + rules + export ~6 wks; A3 statutory duty for est. tens of thousands of firms but low search; P3 Shopify App Store, accountants; M3 packaging weight library, but Valpak already has a large SKU database; W4 producers already pay schemes and fees
platform_distribution: Shopify App Store; accountants and bookkeepers for ecommerce brands; trade associations (FDF, BRC members); Google SEO ('EPR small producer data')
tam_source: bottom-up: est. 40,000 UK small and lower-mid obligated producers × est. 25% adoption × £450 avg ≈ £4.5M (est.)
competitors: Valpak (compliance scheme + EPIC data service); other compliance schemes (Ecosurety, Comply Direct); ecocomply.ai; Unpac; spreadsheets and consultants
competitor_gap: Schemes bundle data services with membership and do not publish prices; enterprise EPR tools target mid-market brands; few tools capture weights from small-batch supplier specs and phone weighing
demand_evidence: GOV.UK guidance sets 1 April 2027 as the deadline for 2026 small-producer data, with £1,303/£696 registration fees and a £386 late fee. Packaging Gateway (Nov 2025) notes small brands face the same packaging rules as global players with no compliance department.
unique_data_capture: Component-level packaging weights and materials for small-brand and generic supplier packaging (mailers, jars, pouches) with sales volumes; improves default weights for every new customer
commoditization_risk: Medium: compliance schemes could release cheaper self-serve tools, and the government reporting service may add templates
regulatory_notes: Producer remains responsible for submitted data; tool must not act as a compliance scheme (which needs approval) and must keep evidence for regulator audits. GDPR minimal.
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible as a UK Ltd selling SaaS; needs periodic checks against changes to EPR reporting codes and an accountant channel for distribution.
mvp_features: Shopify/Excel SKU and sales import; supplier spec and invoice extraction; phone-guided sample weighing; material and class code suggestions; EPR report export with evidence log; deadline and threshold tracker
tech_stack: Next.js + Supabase + Shopify API + OCR + LLM API (Claude/GPT)
review_notes: Crowded with schemes and EPR SaaS; must win on price and ease for small producers or it becomes a feature of a compliance scheme.
